slides.title: Raw data has arrived. What comes first?

slides.title: Turn a file into a trustworthy table
slides.subtitle: Source → structure → import → inspect. Then decide what needs cleaning.

slides.title: Import a CSV into a DataFrame
slides.subtitle: Follow the Demo notebook: import Pandas, read the file, then inspect the table.
notes: Import the library once in the current runtime.
Assign the table to df so later cells can reuse it.
Check column names and the first five records.

slides.title: Excel: choose the right worksheet
slides.subtitle: A workbook can contain several tables. sheet_name=1 selects the second sheet.
notes: The first worksheet is Instructors.
The second worksheet is Courses.
Python uses zero-based worksheet positions: 0, 1, …

slides.title: Check the size. Preview the records.
slides.subtitle: Confirm that the imported DataFrame looks like the source you expected.
notes: shape returns (rows, columns), not a count of cells.
head() defaults to the first five records.
head(3) changes the preview without changing df.

slides.title: Check completeness and data types
slides.subtitle: Missing values and unexpected types change what your analysis can tell you.
notes: count() counts non-null values separately for each column.
info() shows column types and non-null counts.
describe() summarizes numeric columns: count, mean, std and quartiles.

slides.title: Inspect first. Analyse with context.
slides.subtitle: The demo gives you a repeatable routine, not just a list of commands.

parts.title: Your dataset: Happiness Survey
parts.subtitle: Repeat the import routine with happiness_survey_data.csv.
notes: Read the country/year structure before interpreting scores.

parts.title: Preview both ends of the DataFrame
parts.subtitle: The Practice notebook asks for the first 10 rows and the last 5 rows.
notes: head(10): first ten rows.
tail(5): last five rows; original row indices are retained.
Question 1: how many rows and columns are present?

parts.title: What does the Happiness Score tell us?
parts.subtitle: Questions 2–3: find the average and the minimum Happiness Score.
notes: Read mean and min in the happiness_score column.
The average excludes missing values.
Report the answer to two decimal places; keep full precision in calculations.

parts.title: Types and missing values matter
parts.subtitle: Questions 4–5: inspect country_name and count the available social_support values.
notes: country_name is stored as object in the supplied Pandas solution.
A non-null count is different from the number of rows.
Compare the social_support count with df.shape[0].
